_comment: TREATMENT ARM. Matches the profile the resident bot fleet actually buys, measured over 2,843 pools
on factory 0x1f7d7550: median seeded quote 1.0 WETH, median seeded token 9.8e10. Five independent
bots bought 0-2% zero-quote pools vs 63-78% zero-quote among the pools they skipped.
NAME AND SYMBOL ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE CONTROL ARM AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. They are what a human,
a scanner and a sniper bot READ, so if the treatment shipped 'Probe Q1'/'PQ1' against the control's
'Probe Q0'/'PQ0' the token itself would announce its treatment assignment and every observation
would be confounded with a visible text difference. Distinctness of the deployed token addresses
comes entirely from the CREATE2 salt block that run-arm.js derives from armId - see the SALT LAYOUT
note there. Do not 'fix' a duplicate-address worry by editing this text.
NOTE the range differs from the control arm and this is FORCED BY V3, not a design choice: a
position holding quote must straddle spot, a token-only position must not. 'Seed quote' and
'straddling range' cannot be separated in a single position, so this tests the BUNDLE - which is
the same bundle the wild pools present.

OPENING TICK 253000 is CALIBRATED, not chosen: at a full range 1 WETH pairs with 1.0001^tick tokens, so matching the observed 1 WETH / 98e9 profile forces tick ~253093, aligned to 253000. A fork rehearsal at tick 206800 seeded only 9.57e8 tokens - 100x short - which would have made the arms differ on token amount as well as quote.
declaredTx: fill in the declareExperiment transaction hash once it is mined. Leaving it null makes
run-arm.js fall back to a scan anchored on the pad's deploy block (scripts/deployment-<chainId>.json)
- never on block 0, which a range-capped paid RPC refuses, making the pre-registration gate fail
CLOSED on a correctly declared experiment.
